configError.Cause: Klipper could not start because it does not understand something in printer.cfg or in a file included there. The original message names the option or section it stumbled over.
configError.Fix: Correct the configuration, then restart Klipper.
configError.Title: There is a mistake in the configuration

emergencyStop.Cause: The printer was stopped on request, by the emergency stop button or an M112 command. Heaters and motors are off.
emergencyStop.Fix: When it is safe to continue, restart the firmware.
emergencyStop.Title: Emergency stop

extrudeBelowMinTemp.Cause: The printer was asked to push filament while the hotend was below its minimum extrusion temperature. Klipper refuses that to protect the extruder.
extrudeBelowMinTemp.Fix: Heat the nozzle to the printing temperature of your filament and try again.
extrudeBelowMinTemp.Title: The nozzle is too cold to extrude

filamentMissing.Cause: The filament sensor "{sensor}" does not detect filament. The spool may be empty, or the filament broke, is stuck or was pulled out.
filamentMissing.Fix: Load filament, then resume the print.
filamentMissing.Title: No filament at the sensor

filamentRunout.Cause: A filament sensor no longer detects filament. The spool is empty, or the filament broke or is stuck.
filamentRunout.Fix: Load new filament, then resume the print.
filamentRunout.Title: The filament ran out

heaterNotHeating.Cause: The heater "{heater}" did not get warmer fast enough, so Klipper stopped as a protection against a heater that is out of control. Common reasons are a loose heater cartridge or thermistor, a broken heater wire, a fan blowing on the nozzle or a heater that is too weak for the target.
heaterNotHeating.Fix: Check that the heater and its thermistor sit firmly and that the wiring is intact. If the hardware is fine, run a PID calibration.
heaterNotHeating.Title: A heater is not heating up as expected

lostCommunication.Cause: Klipper stopped getting answers from the controller board "{mcu}". Typical reasons are a loose or damaged USB or CAN cable, electrical interference from heater or stepper wiring, or a board that lost power or reset itself.
lostCommunication.Fix: Check the cable and the power supply of the board, then restart the firmware.
lostCommunication.Title: The connection to the controller board was lost

mcuUnableToConnect.Cause: Klipper could not connect to the controller board "{mcu}". The board may be switched off or unplugged, or the serial port or CAN ID in printer.cfg does not match the board.
mcuUnableToConnect.Fix: Make sure the board is powered and connected, check its section in printer.cfg, then restart the firmware.
mcuUnableToConnect.Title: Klipper cannot reach the controller board

moveOutOfRange.Cause: The printer was told to move to a position outside the limits set in printer.cfg. This usually comes from a model placed outside the bed, a slicer profile for a different bed size, or start G-code that moves further than the printer can.
moveOutOfRange.Fix: Check the bed size and the start G-code in your slicer, and the position_min and position_max values in printer.cfg.
moveOutOfRange.Title: A move would leave the printable area

mustHomeFirst.Cause: A move was requested before the printer knew where its axes are. The position is lost whenever the motors are switched off, after a restart and after an error.
mustHomeFirst.Fix: Home all axes and try again. If this happens at the start of a print, add G28 to your start G-code.
mustHomeFirst.Title: The printer has to be homed first

thermistorOutOfRange.Cause: A temperature reading was outside the allowed range, so Klipper switched everything off. Most often a thermistor wire is broken, loose or shorted, or the wrong sensor type is configured. It also happens when a heater really gets hotter than its max_temp.
thermistorOutOfRange.Fix: Check the wiring and plugs of the thermistors on the hotend and the bed, then restart the firmware.
thermistorOutOfRange.Title: A temperature sensor reported an impossible value

timerTooClose.Cause: Klipper could not send its commands to the controller board "{mcu}" in time and stopped the printer to be safe. This usually means the host computer (for example the Raspberry Pi) was overloaded, too hot, short on power or slowed down by a failing SD card.
timerTooClose.Fix: Check the host for heavy load, overheating and an unstable power supply, then restart the firmware.
timerTooClose.Title: The printer's computer could not keep up

unknown.Cause: Mainsail has no explanation for this message yet. This is what Klipper reported:
unknown.Fix: The Klipper log usually shows what happened right before the error.
unknown.Title: The printer reported an error
